title: [Web] Textinput is placed with offset above the keyboard when focused
body: I built a Flutter web app with an editable field at the bottom of the screen. On a mobile browser, tapping the field opens the keyboard, but the app content is moved too far upward and leaves extra space between the field and the keyboard. I can reproduce it with a CanvasKit web build on Safari. The field should align directly above the keyboard.

symptoms_visible: When I focus the bottom editable field in the mobile web app, the keyboard opens but the content moves too far upward, leaving extra space between the field and the keyboard.
N0.label: N0 mobile web keyboard offset reported

symptoms_visible: I see the extra space on physical iPhones and Android devices as well as in a simulator.
On some devices it appears only after repeated taps, and it is more likely when the field has to be moved upward to remain above the keyboard.
N1.label: N1 physical and cross-platform reproduction established

symptoms_visible: The extra keyboard spacing still occurs after setting resizeToAvoidBottomInset to false.
N1_x.label: N1_x resize setting aftermath

symptoms_visible: The HTML-renderer build has the same extra space above the keyboard.
The offset also appears in mobile web browsers on Android, although its frequency varies by device and page complexity.
N2.label: N2 renderer-independent mobile web reproduction

symptoms_visible: The keyboard offset still happens in an app that does not programmatically request focus.
N2_x.label: N2_x focus workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: After dismissing the virtual keyboard with its own control, the page can retain the wrong height and display blank or displaced space.
In the bad state, my logged MediaQuery size changes from 412 by 770 to 412 by 458 and the bottom view inset becomes -312.
N3.label: N3 bad post-keyboard geometry captured

symptoms_visible: On an updated Flutter build, the field and page return to the correct position when the mobile keyboard opens and closes.
I no longer see the extra white space on the physical Pixel test device; the latest master build also works in the tested Android web configuration.
N4.label: N4 corrected viewport behavior verified

symptoms_visible: After updating Flutter, mobile web text fields remain directly above the virtual keyboard and the page geometry resets correctly when the keyboard closes.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Does this also happen on physical devices rather than only in a simulator?
Which physical iOS or Android devices reproduce the offset?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I have the same issue on physical iPhones, including iPhone 14 and iPhone 10, and on a participant10 S22 Ultra. Other affected devices include Pixel and Galaxy models.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I can reproduce it only in the simulator; every physical phone positions the field correctly.
I reproduce it on different recent iPhone and Galaxy models, but not on every tap.

question_patterns: Does it happen on every focus attempt or only intermittently?
Do repeated taps or scrolling make the issue easier to reproduce?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It varies by device. On some real devices it is intermittent and may need repeated taps, while on slower Android devices or more complex pages it happens much more often.

edges.comment: Physical-device reports and intermittent reproduction from c1, c5, c12-c18 and c24 are folded into one simulated user side. Two screenshots: participant5's physical Galaxy Tab A7 Lite reproductions (c14), folded into the merged user side (distinct from the iPhone/S22 devices named in the answer).

solution.intent: Treat the offset as ordinary Scaffold keyboard resizing and disable automatic bottom-inset resizing.
solution.concrete_example: Set Scaffold(resizeToAvoidBottomInset: false) so the Scaffold does not resize when the keyboard appears.

edges.comment: The reporter had already tried this in c3, and multiple later users reported that it did not resolve the issue. It may be part of an Android-web configuration after the framework fix, but it is not the root fix.

question_patterns: Can you build with the HTML renderer and check whether the offset still occurs?
Is the behavior specific to CanvasKit, or can you reproduce it with an HTML-renderer build too?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I just created an HTML build and got the same result. The issue also appears on a physical Android device, although more rarely there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The HTML-renderer build always works correctly; only CanvasKit produces the extra offset.
Both renderers reproduce it, but the frequency is lower with the HTML renderer.

edges.comment: Renderer comparison requested in c6 and performed in c7. The answer reports only the observed build result; it does not infer a framework mechanism.

solution.intent: Avoid calling requestFocus or using autofocus on mobile web and treat duplicate focus requests as the complete cause of the keyboard offset.
solution.concrete_example: On mobile web, skip the post-frame FocusScope.requestFocus call and let the user tap the field to focus it.

edges.comment: Avoiding duplicate requestFocus calls helped the variants reported in c52-c53, but c55 and c77 show that the general issue also occurs without programmatic focus. It is therefore not the case-wide root fix.

question_patterns: Can you log MediaQuery size and viewInsets before and after dismissing the virtual keyboard with the keyboard's own control?
What screen geometry does Flutter report when the page is left in the displaced state?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When I dismiss the keyboard by defocusing, the metrics look normal: Size(412.0, 770.0) with bottom inset 312.0. But if I dismiss it using the control inside the keyboard, I get Size(412.0, 458.0) and EdgeInsets(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, -312.0).

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The size returns to 412 by 770 and the bottom inset returns to zero immediately, even while the visible blank space remains.
I get the same height reduction and negative inset, but my keyboard height is 300 instead of 312 pixels.

edges.comment: The raw geometry values come from c100. Identifying them as stale or incorrectly restored viewport geometry is engineer-side inference and is reserved for the final solution.

question_patterns: Can you update to Flutter 3.38.6 or a newer build containing PR 179581 and retest on the physical device?
Please test the latest Flutter master or fixed stable build and verify that opening and dismissing the keyboard no longer leaves the offset.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the latest published Flutter on Chrome on a physical Pixel 8 and the issue is resolved for me. I also tested the updated master build and the keyboard spacing works correctly; for that Android web Scaffold setup I disabled resizeToAvoidBottomInset.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The fixed build still produces the same negative inset and extra white space on the physical Pixel.
The stable fixed build and current master both work; I verified on a different physical Android model.

edges.comment: Verification from c109-c113 is folded into one simulated user side. This is a test-build/update measurement: users report only that the visible problem is gone in the tested configurations.

solution.intent: Update to a Flutter release containing the mobile-web viewport geometry fix from PR 179581, first shipped on stable in 3.38.6, and verify keyboard opening and dismissal on the affected physical devices.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade Flutter to stable 3.38.6 or newer, rebuild the web app, and retest focus plus keyboard dismissal on the affected mobile browsers. PR 179581 corrects the mobile-web geometry handling that could leave a reduced viewport height and negative bottom inset after the virtual keyboard changed state. If the Android web layout intentionally handles its own keyboard space, keep resizeToAvoidBottomInset disabled for that Scaffold, but do not treat that setting alone as the framework fix.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied raw geometry values, including the reduced height and -312 bottom inset. Engineers connected that evidence to issue 175074 and PR 179581. Naming Flutter's incorrect restoration of mobile-web viewport geometry after virtual-keyboard transitions is therefore an inference from the logs and the verified fixed build, not a conclusion supplied by the reporter.

edges.comment: The thread identifies PR 179581 as the fix and notes that it was cherry-picked to stable 3.38.6. Multiple affected users then verified corrected behavior on current Flutter builds.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as Flutter mobile web mishandling viewport geometry across virtual-keyboard transitions, which could leave a reduced viewport height and a stale or negative bottom view inset and therefore displace the canvas or text field.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the cross-renderer physical-device reproduction and the captured bad metrics, including the height changing from 770 to 458 and the bottom inset becoming -312 after keyboard dismissal.
Must recommend updating to a Flutter release containing the mobile-web viewport geometry fix, then rebuilding and testing the affected mobile web app.

Must not present resizeToAvoidBottomInset=false or avoiding requestFocus as the general root fix: both were insufficient for affected variants, though the Scaffold setting may remain part of a specific Android web layout configuration after updating.
Must require verification on an affected physical mobile browser before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Flutter application developer who can provide minimal Dart reproductions, build with different web renderers, deploy test pages, inspect MediaQuery values, and test across physical iOS and Android devices.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and persistent; gives short factual test results, supplies code and recordings, and distinguishes intermittent device behavior from consistently reproducible configurations. Multiple affected developers are folded into one simulated user side.
